content: If a sponsor plans to conduct a study that is not included in the protocol already submitted as part of their Investigational New Drug (IND) application, they are required to submit a protocol amendment to the FDA. This amendment must include a copy of the new protocol and a concise description of the most clinically significant differences between the new protocol and the previously submitted protocols. A sponsor of an IND application must also submit a protocol amendment if there are changes to the existing protocol that significantly impact the safety of study participants, the scope of the investigation, or the scientific quality of the study. The amendment should provide a brief description of the changes and reference the original protocol submission, including its date and number. Examples of changes that necessitate a protocol amendment include the following: Any increase in the drug dosage or the duration of exposure for individual subjects beyond what is described in the current protocol, or any significant increase in the number of subjects being studied. Any substantial modification to the protocol design, such as the addition or removal of a control group. The introduction of a new test or procedure aimed at improving monitoring for, or reducing the risk of, a side effect or adverse event, or the removal of a test intended to monitor safety. It is important to note that a protocol change intended to address an immediate hazard to human subjects may be implemented immediately. However, the FDA must be notified of this change through a protocol amendment, and the reviewing Institutional Review Board (IRB) must also be informed. Additionally, a sponsor must submit a protocol amendment when a new investigator is added to carry out a previously submitted protocol. This amendment should include the investigator's name, their qualifications to conduct the investigation, and any reference to the previously submitted protocol, if applicable. The FDA must be notified of the addition of the new investigator within 30 days.
